speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that; can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, such as its color, shape, and whether it is itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the rash appeared in specific patterns like collarettes of scale, and are there any crusts or bleeding when the skin is scraped? Also, how is his feeding and general activity level?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis. While the father has psoriasis, the clinical presentation of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead, which worsen in cold weather, is classic for cradle cap/seborrheic dermatitis. I will not order further tests as this is a clinical diagnosis, but please ensure the family understands that cold weather exacerbations are common in this condition.
